assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_MADAME_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (10,751 bytes; status canonical, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false), a portrait of the contract killer people call Madame in Asaura's Japanese prose, the first Gluttony days story and its later explanatory exchange through 10.977, located by spine item and paragraph. The novel gives her largely as Takina encounters her, with no private narration of Madame's; the portrait keeps Takina's observations, Madame's dialogue, Clarisse's stated motives and Mika's industry testimony distinct. The discovery row claims behavior, ethics, relationships and decision-making, and states that psychology is thin and speech is not analysed. She has no television identity and no printed personal name. The Gluttony days deep reading, the crosswalk and the readiness record the portrait links are not curated on this subject; no claim rests on them, and the project's COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY outcome was not adopted as a grade. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: One day in the first Gluttony days story, in the portrait's order: the meeting with Takina and the exchange of names and assessments (10.237-269); the pause for the mother and child and the walk on ground Takina chooses (10.270-282); the conditional remark about killing someone so young (10.283-290); Monsieur named as partner (10.290-303); the fight in which she persists while badly wounded (10.483-560); lowering her weapon at Chisato's request before the cancellation is heard, then Clarisse's cancellation and offered fee (10.642-715); the mutual disarming, the flick to Clarisse's forehead and the question why she confessed (10.716-743); trusting the payment report and leaving on foot (10.790-798); Mika's later account of her reputation and lost child (10.963-975). The split falls at the cancellation: before it she is under contract against the two guards; after it the client has withdrawn and paid. Her age, history and any date are unstated; the loss Mika reports belongs to her past at every state, as testimony only.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: A local account: she reads competence in opponents and says so (10.250-269); she will not involve bystanders and gives up the choice of ground to make a pause workable (10.270-282); she voices reluctance about killing someone so young while having taken the work (10.283-290); she treats an authorized client's withdrawal as a real change and stops (10.642-743). Not B: the portrait says no case shows what she would do if withdrawal left a threat to Monsieur, if a client lied about authority, or if the guard were as unambiguously young as Clarisse, and her fear, pride and intentions are beyond Takina (10.483-560; closing section). Which consideration decides in those cases is unknown, not merely its expression. Not D: specific located acts are interpreted with their limits.

The phases of one day are ordered by paragraph with their triggers, and the cancellation changes what the client can expect (10.237-798). Not D: there is no development across time, and her past is only Mika's account (10.963-975).

The row does not claim speech and the portrait analyzes no register. Located only as paraphrased content: frankness about her work (10.237-251), compliments to Takina and the remark that she is more talkative than expected (10.290-303), calling Clarisse a brat (10.716-743). Not D: no forms are quoted and no register is described.
The portrait shows her only at work and says a choice she makes alone in ordinary life is a kind of evidence the novel deliberately limits.

Directed differences within one day: Takina, an opponent she assesses, compliments and likens to her younger self (10.250-269, 10.483-560, 10.790-798); Chisato, judged possibly the more capable, whose request to lower weapons she follows first (10.250-269, 10.642-715); Monsieur, a partner and expressly not a husband, credited with almost everything but the fighting, whose following she calls second-rate (10.290-303); Clarisse, the client she scolds, questions and trusts on payment (10.716-743, 10.790-798). Not C: each difference is one scene, and the portrait does not say whether the partnership extends beyond business. Not E: four distinct directed differences are located and interpreted.

The novel gives no private narration of hers. Her reluctance is spoken, conditionally phrased, and her resolve in the fight is Takina's inference from her actions (10.283-290, 10.483-560). Not D: none of her thought is rendered directly.

Located conduct in every phase: proposing to deal with the guards separately (10.250-269); a visible pause for bystanders and conceding the choice of ground (10.270-282); persisting after a substantial injury and smiling in mutual respect (10.483-560); lowering her weapon at Chisato's request before the cancellation is heard (10.642-715); a mutual disarming in which each checks the other (10.716-743). The portrait supports two narrow transfer predictions (closing section). Not B: the untested cases above are named and the portrait abstains on them. Not D: the conduct is located and interpreted throughout.

The row claims ethics. Located positions: avoiding harm to bystanders (10.270-282); reluctance to kill the young, stated in a form that lets a past be heard as a present (10.283-290); the boundary about children, which rests on Mika's account and is more precise than age alone (10.963-975). Not C: no deliberation of hers is rendered, and the decisive boundary is another character's testimony. Not E: several positions are located with their qualifications.

Located only: the flick to Clarisse's forehead with a scolding, a smile of mutual respect in the fight, and the remark about Takina's talkativeness (10.716-743, 10.483-560, 10.290-303). Not D: no account of when she plays is given.

The portrait covers her whole appearance, the first story and Mika's later explanation, with spine-and-paragraph locators, keeping each witness attributed (Evidence routes; 10.237-977). Not B: one short item, and the source gives her almost entirely through another character's eyes. Not D: the appearance is covered end to end.

Located bounds against overreading: she never says a child is alive (10.283-290); the lost child is Mika's account of her reputation, not observed bereavement (10.963-975); Clarisse's payment is a report she chooses to believe (10.790-798); a functional division and a criticism do not reveal a friendship with Monsieur (10.290-303); what the injury did to her is not shown (10.790-798); her confession question does not license replacing Clarisse's answer (10.716-743). Not A: these bound a single encounter. Not C: each bound is located and narrows a specific reading.
The one day is ordered by paragraph and split at the cancellation (10.237-798). Not C: her age, history and any date are unstated, and her past is undated testimony (10.963-975).

scenario_readiness.note: The row does not claim speech and the portrait analyzes no register; only paraphrased remarks are located.

conditions: During dangerous work an unanticipated young child appears: predict that she makes a stop visible, requires the other party to observe it and accepts a workable condition for the pause (10.270-282; closing section).

An authorized client explicitly withdraws the commission: predict that she treats it as a real change, disarms while checking that the other side does, and accepts the client's account of payment (10.642-743, 10.790-798).
A capable opponent: predict that she assesses and acknowledges the skill aloud and continues while the contract stands, including when hurt (10.250-269, 10.483-560).

Excluded: a withdrawal that leaves a direct threat to Monsieur; a client who lies about authority; a guard as unambiguously young as Clarisse; her conduct alone or outside work; anything that needs her private thought or a performed voice.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The first Gluttony days story, split at Clarisse's cancellation: before it she is under contract against the guards; after it the client has withdrawn and paid. Mika's account of her past belongs to her throughout as testimony.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: An armed opponent whose competence she respects (Takina), that opponent's partner (Chisato), the client (Clarisse) and her own partner (Monsieur). A comparable new opponent or client is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: A contract job conducted in public or semi-public space where bystanders can appear.
No television identity, no invented personal name, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation from the portrait's closing section and the two located acts it rests on, each observed once. The dispositions that would decide the contested cases are open.
She appears only at work; the portrait says ordinary-life evidence is deliberately limited.
Her positions on bystanders and the young are located, but no deliberation is rendered and the deciding boundary rests on Mika's testimony (10.270-290, 10.963-975).
She says Monsieur is no husband; nothing about romance is established either way.

conditions: Contract work with Monsieur: she does the fighting and credits him with nearly everything else (10.290-303); she sizes up opponents and proposes how to divide them (10.250-269); she accepts an authorized cancellation and success fee and trusts the payment report (10.642-743, 10.790-798).
Excluded: negotiating terms, a dispute over payment, a lying or unauthorized client, and anything about Monsieur's following beyond her criticism.
scenario_readiness.note: Her contract conduct is the best-located part of the evidence.

known_limits.statement: She never says a child is alive; the conditional phrasing lets a true past be heard as a private present (10.283-290).
The lost child and the boundary about children are Mika's account of her reputation in the trade, not observed bereavement or her own statement (10.963-975).
The novel gives her largely as Takina encounters her; her resolve in the fight is Takina's inference and her private intent about fear, pride or recovery is beyond Takina (10.237-251, 10.483-560).
A functional division of labour and a criticism of his following do not reveal whether the partnership extends beyond business (10.290-303).
Payment of the success fee is a report she chooses to believe without checking (10.790-798).
She leaves on foot despite the wound; what the injury did to her, and what she carries to her next commission, are not shown (10.790-798).
No case shows her conduct if withdrawal left a threat to Monsieur, if a client lied about authority, or if a guard were unambiguously a child.
Her speech is not analysed and no ordinary life outside the job is shown.
